chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (mercy of Allah be upon him) said: Muhammad ibn Abu 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Baghdadi related to me on the authority of Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad (peace be upon them), that he said:

O Allah! The imaginations of the imaginative are astonished; the curiosity of the curious has failed; the descriptions of the describers are ruined; and the words of the vain doers have faded in their attempts to perceive You, or to reach Your loftiness. So You are in the place that is not bounded, and the eyes cannot reach You with indication or expression. Far off, then far off! O First One, O Unique, O Incomparable! You are Exalted in loftiness with the Might of Pride, and You are Lofty behind every depth and end with Power and Pride.

key_terms.طَرَفُ الطَّارِفِينَ: curiosity of the curious (literally: the glance of those who look)

ai.seo_question: What does this Shia hadith say about the limits of human description of God?
ai.summary: This supplication from Imam Ali ibn Muhammad (AS) articulates the Shia doctrine of *tanzih* (divine transcendence), asserting that God's essence is beyond the reach of human imagination (*wahm*) and linguistic description. It highlights the epistemological limits of created beings, affirming that while we can recognize His attributes, His true reality remains inaccessible to finite perception, a key theme in al-Saduq's theological framework.
